recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. Future editorial work could fill or remove the placeholder string-handling subsection on resource-formats.html, but that is not required for FHIR-32800 and would be broader than this reconciliation.
issue_request: FHIR-32800 was a Published FHIR-I change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5, asking to clarify string handling for low Unicode code points and to document JSON/XML differences for leading/trailing whitespace, leading zeros, XML comments, and digital-signature canonicalization consequences.
initial_application: Commit 76bb95d2eb022c79180c7cbaf83a9b4be431aeaf explicitly applied FHIR-32800 by adding the parser/serializer MAY retain, escape, or strip language to source/datatypes.html. Commit c97b471ed7602c78c16ad0d68daba08be8783afc, tagged for related Published issue FHIR-18449, added the JSON/XML comparison bullets and canonicalization warning now satisfying the serialization-difference portion of the FHIR-32800 resolution.
additional_context: The maintained JSON/XML comparison section now lives in source/resource-formats.html, and both source/xml.html and source/json.html link readers to resource-formats.html#comparison. FHIR-I WGM minutes for May 2021 confirm the same FHIR-32800 motion and resolution language. Direct Zulip search for the seed found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source files were changed. The current datatype source already includes the approved unsupported-Unicode parser/serializer behavior, and the current shared resource formats page already documents the requested JSON/XML serialization differences and digital-signature ramifications.
